scope: Proposition 8.1 (Gap closure) of the manuscript “Square-lattice FK interfaces and nested loops for 1 <= q < 4” (preprints/Square-lattice-FK-interfaces-and-nested-loops-for-1-leq-q-lt-4-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 223 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d2ffa94ece599e88), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 52. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Keep the distant charges and their locations fixed. Let g denote the gapped wall and f the wall obtained by closing the specified h-gaps, retaining any other gaps and tip factors. There are positive probe-independent numbers bn, bounded above and below, such that Hg(z, u) = bnHf (z, u) + o(1) (8.2) uniformly on interior compact probe sets. The error vanishes in the mesh limit followed by h → 0. Constants may depend on the fixed remaining features. In particular, a second, smaller collection of gaps may be closed before the first collection.
